artworks.title: Amusing Dance - Saukie
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: The image shows a group of eight full-body depictions of Native American men standing and walking together. They are positioned in a line with subtle variations in stance and direction, indicating movement. The men have distinct facial features with dark, straight hair adorned with red and black feathers. Their hair is styled into mohawks or pulled back. They are wearing traditional attire, including fringed skirts, beaded necklaces, and bracelets. One of the men is holding a spear, while another holds a circular shield decorated with patterns, and a smaller hand-held fan-like object. Some men have bows and arrows. The men are set against a light background with pastel tones. The scene is framed with a simple grey-green matte.

artworks.title: Slaves' Dance - Saukie
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: This is a painting showing a group of people dancing or engaging in a ritual near some tipis. The individuals are dressed in traditional clothing and headdresses, dancing energetically in a circle on a grassy field. In the background, tipis are lined up with geometric patterns, supported by long wooden poles. This painting depicts a scene from a Native American cultural event, emphasizing the detailed representation of clothing and communal interaction. The style is reminiscent of George Catlin, who documented scenes from the lives of Native American tribes during the 19th century.

artworks.title: Eagle Dance - Choctaw
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: This is a painting of a group of individuals in a circular formation surrounded by tipis. The scene captures the individuals sitting and standing in a communal setting, engaged in what appears to be a ceremonial performance or gathering. The group is surrounded by tipis against a backdrop of trees and a sky with hues of blue and pink. The figures are detailed with attention to their clothing and body posture, emphasizing community and cultural expression. The style is reminiscent of George Catlin.

artworks.title: Dance to the Berdache - Saukie
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: This is a painting of a group of people clustered together and facing different directions. Many of them have their knees bent. The group stands on light green grass under a blue sky, and the composition is framed in an oval. Almost all of the people are bare chested, their tan skin decorated with horizontal lines of bright red paint. They wear orange and yellow belts and long, white-and-black feathers around their waist. Some wear pants that appear to have tassels or string attached to the sides, while others have bare legs decorated with more red paint. They wear long strands of necklaces and multiple earrings featuring bright turquoise beads, and their hair is tied back in long, thin braids with more feathers and red spikes sticking up from headdresses they wear. Some of the people hold objects like spears, bows, and instruments. One person on the right is dressed differently, wearing a plain brown dress. This person has long black hair, and their body is turned to the left while their face is turned over their shoulder toward us, their eyes closed. In front of the group of people is a semi-circle of gray stones, within which are three large pots or vessels.

artworks.title: Bear Dance - K'nisteneux
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: The image shows a group of Native American men gathered closely together in a dance formation. They are positioned facing slightly towards the right, with their full bodies visible. Some have bent knees and various arm poses suggesting movement. Their faces are visible, featuring a range of expressions, adorned with body paint and feathers. The men have long, dark hair styled with feathers. They are dressed in natural-colored, fringed garments decorated with feathers and painted designs. The background consists of softly blended earth tones transitioning to a lighter blue sky, with green grass beneath their feet.

artworks.title: Discovery Dance - Saukie
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: This is a painting of a group of figures arranged in a circular formation. The figures are painted with vibrant red hues on their heads, carrying spears or sticks. The background is light tan with hints of blue and green. The style of the figures and their attire imply a cultural or historical narrative. The painting is in the style of George Catlin.

artworks.title: Snow Shoe Dance - Ojibbeway
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard

artworks.title: Ball-Play Dance - Choctaw
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: The painting depicts a ceremonial gathering from an elevated perspective. The horizon line is high, showing a wide area with green hills, trees, and a vast sky with clouds. The brushwork is detailed, focusing on figures in ceremonial attire. The color palette is earthy with shades of green and brown. Groups of people are gathered, some on horseback or performing rituals. The artwork is contained within an oval frame on the canvas.

artworks.title: Gathering Wild Rice - Winnebago
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: The image displays a landscape with Native Americans paddling canoes through a marshy field. The point of view is elevated, offering a broad look over the scene. The horizon line is high, just below the sky meeting gentle hills in the distance, with a line of trees along the horizon. The painting style is detailed with fine brushstrokes to convey texture and depth. The color palette is muted, dominated by greens, browns, and blues, with hints of grey and white. Rich vegetation frames the scene, with an expansive and calm sky above.

artworks.title: Fort Pierre
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: The image shows a landscape with tepees spread across a plain. The sky meets the rolling hills in the background. The colors are muted earth tones with soft blues and greys. There are figures and horses on the hills.

artworks.title: Facsimile of an Ojibbeway Robe
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: The painting features various natural symbols and animals on a stretched canvas-like background. The animals, including a buffalo, fox, deer, owl, dog, heron, and others, are drawn in a stylized manner. The background resembles a piece of parchment or animal skin. Symbols such as the sun, moon, and various tools or weapons are also included, giving the image cultural significance. This is in the style of Native American ledger art or similar ethnographic illustrations.

artworks.title: Salmon Spearing - Ottowas
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: The image shows a nighttime landscape with a river extending towards the horizon. There are trees and foliage in the foreground, and the scene is illuminated by scattered fires casting a reddish glow. The color palette includes deep shades of blue and black. The sky and water are depicted with smooth, flowing brushwork.

artworks.title: Funeral of Black Hawk - Saukie
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: The image shows a forest scene with a thick canopy of tall trees. A group of stylized figures are gathered around an area framed by trees and partially obscured structures. The brushstrokes are fine and detailed, especially in the depiction of trees and foliage. The color palette consists of earthy tones of greens and browns with subtle variations capturing the filtered light. The gathering conveys a focused subject amid the natural setting, with figures adorned in attire suggesting a cultural or ceremonial context.

artworks.title: War Dance of the Saukies
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: The painting depicts a scene from an elevated point of view, showing a gathering of people. The horizon is visible above the midway point of the image, with teepees, small buildings, and trees in the background. A group of individuals wearing red headdresses is gathered in a circular pattern, engaging in a dance or ritual. A horseback rider is present, possibly leading the event. In the distance, figures are near a small cabin-like structure, with others gathered on the roof. The brushstrokes are precise, capturing the shapes and details of the scene. The color palette consists of earthy tones, red headdresses, and a blue sky with clouds.

artworks.title: Three Navaho Indians
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: The image depicts three individuals standing in a natural setting. The first person, on the left, wears a garment with a sun-like pattern along the hem and has long, dark hair. The second and third individuals, partially clothed with torsos exposed and wearing jewelry, have markings on their legs and long, dark hair. The central individual wears a feather headdress and crosses their arms, while the person on the right holds a bow and arrows. The background shows rolling hills under a cloudy sky in soft pastel colors.

artworks.title: Apachee Chief and Three Warriors
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: There are four individuals shown standing in a line. Three individuals are facing each other, while one is slightly turned to the side. The central figure is wearing a wrapped garment with a decorative belt and fringed details, while the others are wearing lower body covering attire with exposed upper bodies. Each person is adorned with body paint, feathers in their hair, and has long, dark hair. Their facial features are detailed. One person is holding a spear with feathers, another has a bow and arrows in a quiver on their back, and the remaining two individuals are holding staffs or spears. The background is a neutral hue with grass beneath their feet.

artworks.title: Four Apachee Indians
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: The image shows four individuals standing. Two figures on the left are men in traditional clothing with feathered headdresses. One is in a red-bordered blanket and the other wears leggings and a sash with spears/staffs. The figure on the far right is a woman holding a baby in a cradleboard, wearing a skirt and shawl. Another male figure in the center wears leggings and holds a bow. The background is lightly painted in blue and green, suggesting a natural setting, with the figures standing on grass.

artworks.title: Two Apachee Warriors and a Woman
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: The image shows three individuals depicted in full body within an oval frame. The person on the left is standing slightly to the side, holding a spear, with their head turned towards the center figure. They have long, dark hair adorned with feathers and wear minimal clothing consisting of a wrapped skirt made of soft material. The middle figure stands facing to their left, draped in a rich brown fur cape and a colorful, patterned pink garment with detailed designs. This person also has long hair with feathers. The person on the right is positioned forward and is dressed in a long-sleeved reddish-brown top and a blue-green skirt, their long dark hair is styled with intricate braiding. Each of the individuals wears beaded jewelry, such as necklaces. The background is a soft landscape with blurred green foliage and a cloudy sky, set within a neutral-toned border.

artworks.title: Four Navaho Warriors
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: The image features four men shown in full-body view. The man on the left stands with his back to the viewer, propping one foot on a rock or mound, leaning slightly forward while holding a spear. He wears a fur garment around his waist. The second man faces the viewer directly, holding a spear in his left hand. The third man stands facing forward but with his body turned slightly sideways, holding a ceremonial staff, with one hand on his chest. The fourth man turns to the right, gesturing with his arm extended, holding a round shield in the other hand and wearing leggings with fringed detail. All the men wear similar hairstyles, long and dark, with feathered adornments. Each is shirtless, highlighting muscular torsos, and they wear accessories such as necklaces or feathers. The background is a simple, subtly colored wash, providing an earth-toned contrast to the figures, with a plain border framing the entire composition.

artworks.title: Flathead Indians
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: This painting shows four people standing by the edge of a body of water, with two of the people close to us and two farther away. They are all facing the left, towards the pale blue water that is framed by large gray rocks. In the pair closest to us, a person is standing with one leg forward, holding a large fish in both hands. They have long, dark hair, and they are wearing several earrings in their visible ear and a skirt made of thin strips of brown fringe or fibers with a colorful yellow-and-red belt. Hanging on their back is a child in cradle, swaddled in tan cloth decorated with colorful yellow bands. Behind them stands another adult who is wrapped in a light-colored blanket with a red stripe along the edges. Below the blanket, they wear tan pants and tan shoes with small dots of yellow, blue, and red. Beside these people, on the grassy ground, is a basket of gray fish. The pair that is farther away is painted with less detail, but one person appears to stand and fire an arrow into the water, while the other sits next to a basket of fish, holding one of the fish up. All of the people have light brown skin and long, dark hair. The setting appears to be outdoors, with a blurred background in shades of green and blue. The painting is surrounded by a border of off-white paper.

artworks.title: Four Flathead Indians
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: The image shows four Native American individuals. Three of them are standing, with one kneeling or sitting on the ground. The central figure, a woman, is standing upright and covered with a draped cloth. Her hair is long and is decorated with two feathers. A young child is standing next to her, visible from the waist up. To the right, a man stands holding a spear in one hand and has a bow slung over his shoulder. His long hair is styled back, and he wears minimal clothing, with a piece of cloth wrapped around his waist. On the left, another figure is seated, holding a wrapped bundle. This seated figure has long hair and appears to be looking at the ground. The figures are barefoot, and the background is a natural landscape with grass and an open sky, featuring soft clouds.

artworks.title: A Flathead Chief with His Family
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: The image shows a group of Indigenous people outdoors near a tent-like structure. One person stands at the center wearing a shawl, necklace, and feathered headpiece. Others are sitting or standing nearby, with a child holding a small stick. In front of them are fish, and in the background, fish are drying on a line near the tent. The setting is a forest with tall trees under a sky.

artworks.title: Nayas Indian Chief, His Wife, and a Warrior
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: The image shows three individuals and a baby. Two men stand side by side wearing animal hide leggings, with one holding a wooden staff. They have long dark hair and calm expressions. One man wears circular earrings and a necklace, and both have feathers in their hair. The woman, standing on the right, wears a white shawl over a blue skirt and a large nose ornament. She carries a swaddled baby on her back. The background shows an open landscape with grass and a cloudy blue sky. The scene is framed within an oval on a rectangular canvas with neutral-colored borders.

artworks.title: Nayas Indians
artworks.medium: oil on card mounted on paperboard
artworks.description: The image shows a teepee and a canoe near a river. The teepee is in the foreground, with its canvas fluttering gently. A canoe is on the water to the right, under a sky with soft pastel tones. Lush trees frame the scene in the background. A rack near the teepee displays items hanging from it. The ground is vibrant with the rustic colors of grass. The style is reminiscent of George Catlin.
